source.title: Adaptive Gradient Methods at the Edge of Stability
source.authors: Jeremy M. Cohen; B. Ghorbani; Shankar Krishnan; Naman Agarwal; Sourabh Medapati; Michal Baďura; Daniel Suo; David E. Cardoze; Zachary Nado; G. Dahl; J. Gilmer

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figure labels are flattened or garbled, but the relevant prose and figure descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training loss and curvature around stability thresholds for adaptive optimizers, addressing the edge-of-stability dynamics in V5 with a different optimizer focus and measures than the cited non-adaptive studies.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper’s own training and curvature measurements. Cited results from earlier work are not included. Several plotted values are figure-only and cannot be read precisely from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Appendix C, Figure 13 directly repeats full-batch non-adaptive gradient-descent experiments measuring Hessian sharpness against optimizer stability thresholds, testing V5's edge-of-stability component. The record incorrectly treats initial-loss recovery as the only testable part of V5. Most adaptive-optimizer results instead concern preconditioned sharpness and do not directly test the stated raw-sharpness claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: full-batch adaptive optimizers typically equilibrate at a preconditioned stability threshold, with related but less uniform minibatch behavior. Adaptive preconditioning can permit increasing raw curvature. The authors acknowledge very-small-learning-rate exceptions and describe the minibatch equilibrium more tentatively.
record.recipe_differences: Studies adaptive optimizer stability and curvature dynamics, rather than the specific non-adaptive learning-rate and sharpness claims in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curvature behavior varies with learning rate, batch size, Adam’s β2, momentum type, warmup, and architecture. Smaller learning rates or smaller β2 are associated with sharper solutions; smaller batches tend to have lower mid-training preconditioned sharpness. The Post-LN Transformer shows late-warmup instability.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-batch adaptive optimizers typically equilibrate in preconditioned sharpness at optimizer-specific thresholds, while raw sharpness can continue increasing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers exhibit an edge of stability defined by the preconditioned Hessian, and adaptation can permit continued movement into regions of higher raw curvature.

fits_no_version.finding: At extremely small Adam learning rates, preconditioned sharpness can remain below the threshold; freezing the preconditioner causes it to rise to the threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive preconditioning can prevent preconditioned sharpness from reaching the frozen-optimizer stability threshold at very small learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: On a scalar quadratic, rmsprop temporarily oscillates explosively at rates unstable for its initial frozen preconditioner, then adaptation halts divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive preconditioning can arrest instability above an initial frozen-preconditioner threshold even on a fixed quadratic.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen Adam on CIFAR-10 reaches an edge of stability measured using a fixed preconditioner.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-batch gradient descent with fixed preconditioning exhibits threshold equilibration in preconditioned Hessian sharpness.

record.problems: Key curvature and loss outcomes are mostly presented in figures without extractable numerical values. The paper describes some observations qualitatively, and notes that Post-LN Transformer training fails late in warmup.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained because the study’s own measurements do not directly establish the specified V5 outcome of training loss recovering to a low value after a learning-rate-induced rise. The paper reports related curvature and loss trajectories in Figures 1–10 and 12–19.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, and dependence on model size, early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for training speed and trainable depth.

The specified wide-network squared-loss catapult regime relative to the initial linearized-model threshold, its larger-rate divergence boundary, and neural-network divergence despite starting below the threshold. Figure 13 directly reports sharpness behavior but does not supply a corresponding loss trajectory establishing the loss-decrease component.
Matched comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

missing.what: Extract the direct non-adaptive V5 results separately by optimizer and learning-rate condition: vanilla GD and Nesterov hover above their thresholds except at the smallest rate, while heavy-ball momentum oscillates around its threshold. Qualitative prose supports extraction without precise graph values.
missing.locator: Appendix C, non-adaptive gradient descent discussion and Figure 13

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for V5. There are no existing rows to fix. Although rows_left_out broadly names Figures 12–19, its justification overlooks Figure 13's direct non-adaptive test; the missing entry identifies this necessary extraction correction. Adaptive preconditioned-sharpness exceptions are not challenges to V5's stated non-adaptive raw-sharpness result.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 fitting, label corruption, and the effects of model size and early stopping are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum or width comparison.
No comparison of plain networks with and without identity shortcuts for training error.
No comparison of initialization schemes for learning speed or trainable depth.

The study measures adaptive optimizers’ curvature and loss dynamics near stability thresholds, but does not test the version’s specific claim about learning rates above the initial linearized-model stability limit producing a brief loss rise followed by low loss. Its measurements are related but do not establish that claim’s specified training-loss outcome.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison of training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.condition: Full-batch training of a five-hidden-layer tanh network on CIFAR-10 using vanilla GD and Nesterov momentum, excluding the smallest learning rate noted in the prose.
relationships.reason: Based on Appendix C, Figure 13 rather than extracted rows: raw Hessian sharpness hovers above the respective stability thresholds during training. This supports V5's sharpness component; no row ids were retained.
relationships.display_finding: Raw Hessian sharpness hovered above the respective GD and Nesterov stability thresholds during training.
